title: Priesthood of all believers
hookLine: Luther stressed that every baptized Christian has a priestly calling (1 Peter 2:9)

lines: A COBBLER, A SMITH, A FARMER.
cards: A cobbler bends over a shoe, stitching by lamplight. A blacksmith sweats at his forge. A farmer walks behind a plow.
In Martin Luther's Germany, people spoke of a spiritual estate, the priests and monks, and a worldly estate, everyone else. Luther disagreed, loudly.

In a letter to the German nobility, he wrote that the cobbler, the smith and the farmer each have the work of their trade, and yet all of them, by baptism, are alike consecrated priests. Not just the priest at the altar.
The cobbler too. He found it in a much older letter.

teach.h: A ROYAL PRIESTHOOD, A HOLY NATION.
teach.b: That older letter is the first letter of Peter: "But ye are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, an holy nation, a peculiar people." Written to ordinary believers, not clergy.
And Peter echoes a far older promise at Mount Sinai, where God tells Israel, "ye shall be unto me a kingdom of priests, and an holy nation."
Jews read that verse as their own calling, and Peter's readers heard themselves invited into its language. So what does a priest do?

A priest stands between: bringing people's needs to God, and God's blessing to people. Peter says this whole people exists to "shew forth the praises of him who hath called you out of darkness into his marvellous light."
Luther pressed it hard. If every baptized person is a priest, no one stands higher before God because of their job. A pastor still serves, for good order, as we saw yesterday.

teach.h: THE COBBLER ON THE SAME GROUND.
teach.b: But a mother changing diapers and a monk saying his prayers stand on the same ground. Protestant teachers built on it a high view of ordinary work as a calling. Other churches read the verse their own way.
Catholic teaching speaks of a common priesthood shared by all the baptized, and a ministerial priesthood of the ordained, different in kind, yet ordered to one another.
Orthodox Christians speak of the royal priesthood of the whole people of God, offering the world back to God in thanksgiving.

teach.h: DO IT HEARTILY, AS TO THE LORD.
teach.b: And a line from Paul for any workbench: "whatsoever ye do, do it heartily, as to the Lord, and not unto men."

how: Protestant churches teach the priesthood of all believers, often with a strong sense of ordinary work as a calling; Catholic teaching speaks of the common priesthood of the baptized alongside the ordained priesthood, and Orthodox Christians speak of the royal priesthood of the whole people of God.

games.q: what does “priesthood of all believers” mean?
o: an order of monks who live and pray together
every baptized Christian sharing a priestly calling
a rule that every believer must lead church services

games.q: who said it, and where — tap the pairs.
p: a royal priesthood, an holy nation
the cobbler too is a consecrated priest
do it heartily, as to the Lord

s: 1 Peter calls only the clergy a royal priesthood
the letter is written to ordinary believers: "ye are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood."
Luther's teaching did away with pastors
pastors still serve, for good order; Luther's point was that no one stands higher before God because of their job.
Peter's phrase echoes God's words at Sinai
"ye shall be unto me a kingdom of priests, and an holy nation."

games.q: you're a cobbler in Luther's town. you've just heard that by baptism you're a consecrated priest. what now?
o: close the shop and enter a monastery.
keep making shoes, and make them well, for your neighbors.
make cheap shoes, since only faith matters.
games.why: Luther said the cobbler, the smith and the farmer each have the work of their trade, and serve others by it. the shoe is the calling.

practice: Bring to mind the next task waiting for you, a shift, a report, a sink of dishes, an email you've been avoiding, and picture the people it touches. Picture doing it for them, carefully, as if it mattered beyond the paycheck.
If you pray, offer the task to God before you start; if you don't, decide who it's really for, and hold that person in mind.

wordCard.voice: The priesthood of all believers. In this teaching, every baptized Christian is called to stand between God and the world, at the altar or the workbench.

orig.note: Greek: a priesthood, a body of priests — the word in 1 Peter 2:9, "a royal priesthood."

carryVoice: Your line: a royal priesthood. At the altar, and at the cobbler's bench. See you tomorrow.
